clue.text: True nature revealed by unruly inquest scene

indicators.note: unruly means disorderly, so the letters of the two following words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A rowdy scene at an inquest exposes what people are really like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unruly' rearranges the twelve letters of INQUEST and SCENE together.
explanation.definitionFit: The essence of a thing, its most perfect embodiment, is its true nature.

clue.text: Roger, noted for making bedcovers?

definitions.meaning: Roger ... was an English composer, and 'noted' hints at musical notes

explanation.surface: A man named Roger is famous for sewing blankets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noted' looks like 'famous' but points to music: Roger Quilter (1877-1953) was an English songwriter.
explanation.definitionFit: The composer's surname, and also the trade name for a maker of padded bedspreads.

clue.text: Perfect" the man with the cards might say

definitions.meaning: perfect as an adjective: flawless, the best imaginable

definitions.text: the man with the cards might say
definitions.meaning: the dealer at a card table announces that it is his turn to hand out the cards

explanation.surface: A card dealer exclaims that something is perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer after its first letter and it is what a dealer says: 'I' plus 'deal'.
explanation.definitionFit: Flawless and exemplary are the same quality; the second reading is the dealer's own claim to the pack.

clue.text: Outward signs are right in séance phenomena

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for right inside the word for the séance noises

parts.note: spirits at a séance traditionally communicate by knocking, so tappings

explanation.surface: Spooky knocks at a séance are said to be outward signs of the dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts R inside TAPPINGS, the knocks heard at a séance.
explanation.definitionFit: Trappings are the external show or ornaments of something, its outward signs.

clue.text: Declared in port

definitions.meaning: Port ... is the Egyptian harbour at the north end of the Suez Canal

explanation.surface: Something was announced in a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of 'say' means stated; it is also the name of the Egyptian harbour city on the Suez Canal.

clue.text: Urge the factory to produce fruitful growth

parts.note: to egg someone on is to urge them
a plant is an industrial works or factory

explanation.surface: Someone presses a factory to raise its output.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Urge' and 'factory' suggest industry; they are just EGG and PLANT, and 'to produce' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The aubergine is a fruiting vegetable plant, so a fruitful growth.

clue.text: Room on board for many a container

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many
a bin is a container

explanation.surface: A ship's room is used to store lots of boxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link: C (Roman 100, 'many'), A and BIN make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A private room for a passenger or crew member aboard a ship.

clue.text: Parisian material includes one architectural feature

indicators.note: includes means the material wraps around the next piece

parts.note: plaster of Paris is a building material, so 'Parisian material' gives plaster
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A French fabric is part of some architectural design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parisian material' sounds like French cloth; it is plaster of Paris. 'includes' puts I inside PLASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectangular column set into a wall as ornament is a classic architectural feature.

clue.text: Flat trees ?

definitions.meaning: flat as a noun: level surfaces, like geometric surfaces with no curve
the plane is a broad-leaved tree, often planted along London streets

explanation.surface: Someone describes a stretch of trees as flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Level surfaces in geometry are flats, and the London street tree shares the name.

clue.text: Repeating that I get a half-term assessment

indicators.note: half of the word term is its first two letters, the opening half

parts.note: a rating is an assessment or valuation

explanation.surface: A pupil says again that they get a report at half-term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-term' looks like a school holiday break, but the hyphen is split: 'half' works on 'term' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing or saying something again and again is reiterating, going over it once more.

clue.text: Transport organization badly needs fish

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the former UK national railway
ill can mean badly, as in ill-treated

explanation.surface: A rail company is in poor shape and needs to buy fish.
explanation.walkthrough: BR was British Rail, Britain's state railway until the 1990s. 'needs' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A flatfish related to the turbot, a species of fish.

clue.text: Flowers Olivia almost itemized as " indifferent red "'?

indicators.note: almost suggests the words only nearly match, a near sound rather than a spelling

parts.note: in Twelfth Night Olivia lists her beauty: 'Item, two lips, indifferent red'

explanation.surface: Olivia counts off her features, describing some flowers as of a so-so red.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's Twelfth Night, Olivia inventories her face: 'Item, two lips, indifferent red'. 'two lips' said aloud is nearly the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Spring bulbs with cup-shaped blooms, a common garden flower.

clue.text: Herb produced by a hill, dweller out of hs element

annotationWithheld.why: Herb produced by a hill-dweller out of his element (8): PLANTAIN is ANT (hill-dweller) inside PLAIN, but no clue word gives PLAIN or signals the insertion; 'out of his element' would have to be both the container and its indicator
annotationWithheld.clue: Herb produced by a hill, dweller out of hs element

clue.text: Mounted in Yorkshire

definitions.meaning: the ... were the three historic divisions of Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Someone is up on a horse in Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire, an English county, was divided into North, East and West Ridings.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on horseback is the equestrian sense; the Yorkshire one is an old administrative division.

clue.text: 2 dn etc possibly describing Agag's gait coming to Samuel

definitions.text: describing Agag's gait coming to Samuel

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: the answer to 2 down, meaning perfect

explanation.surface: A biblical note on how King Agag walked up to Samuel.
explanation.walkthrough: In 1 Samuel 15:32 'Agag came unto him delicately'. 'possibly' rearranges IDEAL (2 down) with ETC.
explanation.definitionFit: The King James Bible says the doomed king approached the prophet in a mincing, dainty manner.

clue.text: Blows up in accommodation around the Eastern Front

indicators.note: around puts the housing word on both sides of the next letter

parts.note: flats are accommodation

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A war report: an explosion near housing on the Eastern Front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eastern Front' summons the Second World War; here 'Front' only picks the opening letter of 'Eastern', and 'in' is taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow up a balloon or tyre is to fill it with air until it swells.

clue.text: Autumn activity stops

definitions.meaning: in autumn trees shed foliage, their leaves coming off
to leave off doing something is to stop

explanation.surface: The work of autumn comes to a halt.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceasing is the idiom's sense; read literally it is trees losing their foliage in the fall.

clue.text: Signs ominous to the French flavouring

parts.note: au is French for 'to the'
spices are flavourings

explanation.surface: Some French seasoning is seen as a bad omen.
explanation.definitionFit: Omens read from the flight of birds by Roman augurs, hence portents.

clue.text: Removal of Niagara from itinerary causes quarrels

definitions.meaning: Niagara Falls struck off the travel plan: the falls are out
to fall out is to quarrel

explanation.surface: Cancelling the Niagara trip starts family rows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'causes' is a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to have a row; literally it is the falls taken off the plan.

clue.text: A move by a man of honour — Bacon perhaps

parts.note: a flit is a move of house, often in secret
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A move made by an honoured man, perhaps Francis Bacon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bacon' looks like the philosopher Francis Bacon; it is cured pork. CH is the Companion of Honour, a British award.
explanation.definitionFit: A side of cured pork is the traditional cut, as in the Dunmow prize.

clue.text: The root of incentive

definitions.meaning: the reward dangled before a donkey

explanation.surface: Someone names the basic source of motivation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'root of' reads as 'source of'; 'of' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The vegetable dangled before a donkey became the byword for a reward that motivates.

clue.text: Had general direction to turn right, then finished

indicators.note: to turn means the abbreviation is flipped round to face the other way

parts.note: ended means finished

explanation.surface: A driver who was heading one way turned right and stopped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn right' reads as a driving instruction, but 'to turn' flips the abbreviation for right; 'then' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tended in a particular way overall; a trend is a prevailing course.

clue.text: Measure cover of rock

parts.note: an inch is a measure of length
a cape is a cloak, a cover

explanation.surface: A measuring cover for a rock.
explanation.walkthrough: The Inchcape Rock is a reef off Scotland, the subject of a Robert Southey ballad. 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bell Rock reef in the North Sea, known from Southey's poem about its warning bell.

clue.text: What is it about a horse that makes it a certainty?

definitions.text: What is it about a horse
definitions.meaning: a saddle girth, which goes around the horse

explanation.surface: Someone asks what about a racehorse makes it a sure bet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' means around: the strap that goes about a horse. 'that makes it' links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A saddle girth in American usage, and informally a sure thing.

clue.text: She sounds flighty

indicators.note: sounds tells us the girl's name is heard as another word

parts.note: the nelly is a giant petrel, a seabird and so able to take flight

explanation.surface: A woman comes across as fickle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flighty' suggests fickle; read it as 'able to fly'. The nelly is a giant petrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name stands for any woman, as the pronoun does.

clue.text: Amount of wine which made the soldiers fiery?

parts.note: lit means set alight, and also drunk
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: How much wine it took to get the troops worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers. LIT means alight and also drunk, which a quantity of wine might make soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A metric unit of volume, about a standard bottle and a third of wine.

clue.text: Put up money in Anglian television

indicators.note: in says the letters sit within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Investors fund a regional TV channel in East Anglia.
explanation.walkthrough: Anglia Television was the ITV franchise for East Anglia; the answer runs across 'anglIAN TElevision'.
explanation.definitionFit: The stake each player puts in the pot before a poker deal.

clue.text: What road-hogs do on the dance floor too?

definitions.text: What road-hogs do on the dance floor too?

parts.words: What road-hogs do on the dance floor too?
parts.note: selfish drivers push into the lane ahead, and at a dance one partner claims another's

explanation.surface: Bad drivers behave just as badly when dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: A road-hog is a selfish driver; the phrase also names interrupting a couple to take over a partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Pushing into a gap in traffic and taking over someone's dance partner share the phrasal verb.

clue.text: Company man with internal injury — all twisted

indicators.note: with internal says the next word sits inside the man's name

parts.note: Ned is a man's name
a tort is a civil wrong, an injury in law

explanation.surface: A firm's employee hurt inside is all bent out of shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'internal injury' looks medical, but a tort is a legal wrong, and 'with internal' sets it inside the man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Bent and wrenched out of shape, as a face in pain.

clue.text: Wrong side? Fletcher might sit on it

definitions.text: Wrong side? Fletcher might sit on it

indicators.note: wrong suggests the letters are in the wrong order and need sorting

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a man called Fletcher is on the wrong side of the furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong' rearranges the two words together; read as a whole, any man called Fletcher might sit on this sofa, so the clue is its own definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep-buttoned leather sofa named after an Earl, a seat for anybody.
